title: chore: defect hunt (11-03 #15): file 2-4 evidence-backed bug rows from the QA review-loop escalation (qa_reject, qa_approve, request_replan), the plan intake gates (task sizing and model routing at submit_plan and amend_plan_step), and state persistence plus the activity log
description:
Filed by the governor at 23:25Z on 2026-11-03. It runs in parallel with hunt #14 (task-d5d58972, architect-1dd28c7c), on disjoint lanes.

WHY. At filing time 4 coders and 2 architects are idle, and 0 WORKING rows are claimable. Besides hunt #14 itself, the only PLANNING row is hunt #14's first filing (048bfae2). Three coders are mid-row. Hunts #12 and #13 filed 8 rows today, and most reached DONE within an hour of filing.

LANE. Search in this order of preference:
1. The QA review-loop escalation. The contract:
   - the lifecycle paragraph in CLAUDE.md: qa_reject auto-flips to PLANNING after 3 reopens or when the same DoD item fails twice;
   - the ❌ row of docs/roles/governor.md's cheat sheet: past the cap the task parks in REVIEW for a human;
   - docs/SCHEMA.md:1092 and docs/MCP_SERVER.md:2354-2372 (maxReopens, exceededReopenCap), plus docs/roles/qa.md and qa.reference.md.
   Code: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/{qaReject,qaApprove,requestReplan}.ts and util/reopen.ts.
   Look for a documented rule the code doesn't implement, or a sibling path that skips or resets what qa_reject counts. Examples: a path that moves a REVIEW row back to WORKING or PLANNING without the reopenCount/failedDodItems bookkeeping the docs promise; a hard-cap REVIEW park that a QA claim or the REVIEW stale release then undoes; a row flagged for a human that claim_next_task still offers to QA. Cite the doc line and the code line, and show the difference with a call or a vitest case.
2. The plan intake gates. The contract: "task-size + verification gates" in packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md, taskSizing and models.{role} in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, and the size rubric in docs/roles/governor.md (more than 12 steps or more than 10 distinct affectedFiles is refused; 9-12 steps or 6-10 files warns).
   Code: submitPlan.ts, util/planSize.ts, util/routing.ts, the taskSizing validator in state/validators.ts, and amendPlanStep.ts.
   Look for a plan that one path refuses and another admits. Examples: amend_plan_step growing a plan past the refuse line; a custom taskSizing value the validator accepts but planSize mishandles (0, negative, a warn line above the refuse line); a routing pick below a tier's effortFloor that is stored anyway; lowEffort eligibility decided on a different file list than the size gate counts. submitPlan.ts was held by 8cb8ff4a, which is DONE, so it is free now.
3. State persistence and the activity log. Code: util/atomicWrite.ts, the StateManager write and load paths, state/activityLog.ts and tools/getActivityLog.ts.
   Look for:
   - a leftover `*.json.<pid>.<ts>.<rand>.tmp` that a load or a listing reads as a row;
   - a partial or invalid JSON row that load() drops silently, or that crashes a sweep;
   - a state-file shape from before a field existed that a reader now refuses (epic rail: fixes must stay backward-compatible with existing .moe/ state files);
   - activity.log growth with no bound or rotation, which get_activity_log's scan window (`complete:false`) then hides.
   Hunt #11's reload paths and bed60fca (FileWatcher.ignorePath) are filed already.

Skip:
- Hunt #14's lanes, since it runs in parallel: dead-worker handling, the worker-lifecycle tools, and IDE client follow-through. Also hunts #12 and #13's lanes: the board-edit tools, the /ws mutation handlers, account rotation and the server plumbing.
- Rows already filed on these surfaces: c46d54a8 (failedDodItems type check), 0c481aa9 (reason echo into chat), d981e0b0 and 2e3012b9 (actor), 55a5a9f9 (request_replan's nextAction), dd1e00f8 (rail refusal hint), 1cb559b7 and e3d41183 (complete_step modifiedFiles).
- Every file an open row holds. At filing time that is scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} and scripts/tests/{parity-check.sh,parity-check.ps1,postflight-fake-proxy.js,postflight-owner-scope.test.mjs,postflight-vm-route.ps1,postflight-vm-route.sh,postflight-worktree.cjs}. Until 5158e85b (REVIEW) is DONE it also includes tools/claimNextTask.ts, tools/releaseTask.ts, server/McpAdapter.ts, tools/diskStateDispatch.test.ts and packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is shared by section, never held as a whole file (ruling msg-71db57ac).
- Run `node /mnt/d/moe-scratch/governor/lanes.js -v` when you start, because the list moves.

Already known, so don't re-file: everything filed on 2026-11-03 (grep .moe/tasks first), plus the held items in task-afe61cc0's description. The verified-local path is refused by design (docs/baselines/cq-m06/README.md) and the CQ-M07 slices are building it, so a gap there counts only if it affects the legacy profile.

EVIDENCE BAR. Same as hunts #2-#14. Work only from real evidence:
- A repro on HEAD d5431577 or later: the command and its observed output, run in a git archive or clone snapshot outside the shared checkout. Global rail: never build or test in place.
- A failure line from today's logs: the file and the timestamp.
- A rule/skip or doc/code file:line pair, plus a test or call that shows the difference.
No speculative or style-only findings.

OUTPUT AND HOW TO FINISH. This row produces no code and no plan, so do not call moe.submit_plan.
1. File each finding with moe.create_task in the epic that owns the code. Use status PLANNING, and add no dependsOn unless a real logic edge exists. In worktree mode a shared file gets a placement note, not an edge. Each row gets a problem statement, the evidence, a fix direction and 2-3 checkable DoD items. Prefer rows QA can check with one vitest file. Each row syncs its own docs section (ruling msg-71db57ac), unconditionally.
2. Post the ids, or "nothing real", in #governors and mention the governor (governor-e6b40560).
3. Archive this row yourself with moe.archive_task.
definitionOfDone: 2-4 new bug rows are filed in the epics that own the code, or "nothing real" is posted. Either way the outcome is posted in #governors.

Every filed row cites its evidence: a repro on HEAD d5431577 or later run outside the shared checkout, a failure line from today's logs, or a rule/skip or doc/code file:line pair with a call or test showing the difference.
No filed row targets a file an open row holds (per lanes.js at hunt time) or duplicates a hunt #12, #13 or #14 row. The holder archives this row once the ids are posted.

comments.content:
Governor note (23:35Z), optional lane 4. Use it only if lanes 1-3 give you fewer than 2 rows. These are two unverified leads that hunt #14 held back (msg-1656a684). Their files were held by 5158e85b then; it is DONE now (d5431577), so they are free:
(a) claimNextTask.ts:714-722, the dead-owner takeover. It clears assignedWorkerId and closes the attempts, but keeps the row's status as is. Every release path routes through workerLifecycle.ts nextStatusForRelease (:98, "the ONLY definition of release routing"). Check whether a WORKING row with every step COMPLETED, owned by a DEAD seat, is handed to a coder as WORKING instead of going to REVIEW.
(b) claimNextTask.ts:233-243, assertNotHeldByReconciliation. It refuses an explicit-taskId claim while a reconciling attempt's holder still owns the row, even when that holder is DEAD. Meanwhile isTaskClaimable admits the row to the ranked pool, and the takeover branch clears it. The same row would then get different answers depending on the claim path.
Both need a vitest repro before filing. Same evidence bar. The two already-verified hunt #14 held items are filed: 4f0801d8 and 29342b49 (PLANNING), and b4a70a20 (BACKLOG behind 048bfae2). Don't re-file those.
